content.user_title: Configure Azure Monitor Telemetry for Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need clear guidance to send traces, metrics, and logs to Azure Monitor. This skill provides setup, span, metric, exception, and migration examples for OpenTelemetry-based observability.
actual_capabilities: Explains that azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter is deprecated and points to autoconfigure migration.
Shows Maven dependency snippets for the deprecated exporter and recommended autoconfigure package.
Demonstrates setup with APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING or an explicit connection string.
Provides Java examples for spans, attributes, nested spans, and exception recording.
Shows OpenTelemetry metric examples for counters and histograms.
Lists reference links for Maven, Azure SDK, OpenTelemetry Java, and Application Insights.
limitations: The referenced exporter package is deprecated, so new projects should prefer autoconfigure.
Examples are illustrative and do not include full application wiring or build files.
The skill does not validate real Azure connection strings or Azure resource permissions.
It does not cover every OpenTelemetry instrumentation library or advanced sampling policy.

use_cases.title: Migrate a Java service
use_cases.description: Plan a move from the deprecated Azure Monitor exporter package to the autoconfigure package.

use_cases.title: Add basic tracing
use_cases.description: Use span and attribute examples to add distributed tracing to a Java operation.

use_cases.title: Improve production diagnostics
use_cases.description: Record exceptions, metrics, and operation context for Azure Monitor troubleshooting.

prompt_templates.title: Start telemetry setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java application
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for a Java service using the recommended autoconfigure package.

prompt_templates.title: Add spans to an operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add OpenTelemetry spans, attributes, and exception recording to a Java method that processes customer orders.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Move away from the deprecated exporter
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the deprecated Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry exporter setup with the autoconfigure approach and give me a migration checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Design observability coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Java observability plan for Azure Monitor that covers traces, metrics, exception recording, span naming, and useful attributes.

output_examples.input: I need to send Java OpenTelemetry data to Azure Monitor.
output_examples.output: The response explains the recommended autoconfigure package, the connection string environment variable, and the basic initialization flow.

output_examples.input: How should I record errors in spans?
output_examples.output: The response describes recording the exception, setting an error status, rethrowing the exception, and ending the span safely.

output_examples.input: What should I change during migration?
output_examples.output: The response identifies the deprecated dependency, recommends autoconfigure, and outlines initialization changes to review.

best_practices: Use the autoconfigure package for new work because the exporter package is deprecated.
Set meaningful span names and include useful attributes for troubleshooting.
Record exceptions and end spans in finally blocks or try-with-resources scopes.
anti_patterns: Starting new projects on the deprecated exporter package.
Using vague span names that do not describe the operation.
Adding sensitive customer data or secrets as span attributes.

faq.question: Is this skill for new Java projects?
faq.answer: Yes, but it recommends the autoconfigure package because the older exporter package is deprecated.

faq.question: Does it include Application Insights setup?
faq.answer: It shows how to use an Application Insights connection string with Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry.

faq.question: Can it help with migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains replacing the deprecated exporter dependency and reviewing initialization code.

faq.question: Does it provide complete runnable projects?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused snippets and guidance that must be adapted to your Java application.

faq.question: Does it cover metrics as well as traces?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for counters, histograms, span creation, attributes, and exception recording.

faq.question: Should I put secrets in span attributes?
faq.answer: No. Keep secrets, credentials, and sensitive customer data out of telemetry attributes.
